questions.q: True or false? The carrier is close, so the nearest midfielder should dive in with a tackle straight away.
questions.explain: Right, it's false. Get close without diving in, so the carrier can't simply go past you.
choiceExplanations: Diving in lets the carrier knock the ball past you. Get close and stay on your feet instead.
Right, it's false. Get close without diving in, so the carrier can't simply go past you.

questions.q: Put the decision after losing the ball in order, from first to last.
options: Look at the carrier and your helpers
questions.explain: Yes. Look first, press while the ball can be won, and recover once the carrier escapes.
choiceExplanations: Yes. Look first, press while the ball can be won, and recover once the carrier escapes.
You approach only after checking the carrier's distance and who covers behind you.
The carrier escaping is the new picture that comes after your first approach.
Recovering is the last step, once the chance to win the ball has gone.

questions.q: Now the carrier escapes past you on the right side. Tap where your recovery run should end.
questions.explain: Yes. Recovering goal side puts you between the ball and goal, so you can help again.
choiceExplanations: Chasing from behind can't stop the carrier, and a tackle from there often becomes a foul.
Waiting up the pitch leaves your team a player short while the carrier runs at goal.
Yes. Recovering goal side puts you between the ball and goal, so you can help again.
